name: Jeshua
bio: Jeshua returned from Babylon to Jerusalem and Judah among the leaders of the first group of exiles under Cyrus's decree, together with Zerubbabel (Ezra 1:11-2:2). As high priest, he is also called Joshua in Haggai and Zechariah; his priestly leadership in rebuilding the temple and the Levitical register tied to his family are told in detail in the chapters ahead. Once settled in their towns, Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, together with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives, rebuilt the altar of the God of Israel despite their fear of the surrounding peoples, resuming burnt offerings and keeping the Feast of Tabernacles, though the temple's foundation was not yet laid. In the second year, they began the work in earnest, appointing Levites twenty and older to oversee it; when the foundation was finally laid, the priests and Levites praised the LORD with trumpets and cymbals as David had ordained, and the people shouted for joy — though many older priests, Levites, and family heads who remembered the first temple wept so loudly that their weeping and the people's shouting could not be told apart (Ezra 3:1-13).
